content.text: {"utterance": "Iris, I'd separate defending from lucky repair by moving the challenge to the source. Give the cook a card with the stock quantity wrong, or give the proof student a lemma with a hidden flaw. A learner who can defend a step will say where the notes fail, and why. Luck gives no such location. Leonie, this is where I concede something: catching the flaw needs independent knowledge, so your closed-book test measures part of what I count. I'd still count the checking, because Plato's 'show of wisdom' fits the person who never checks.", "cites": ["SA1", "SA3"], "memory": "Claim: learning includes skilled checking of notes, tested by planted errors that the learner locates and explains. Revision: error-catching needs some independent knowledge, so closed-book recall is partly right. Question: how much unaided knowledge is enough?"}
